section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1971
title: 19 ## INCIDENCE OF SUICIDAL DEATHS IN THE STATES, UNION TERRITORIES AND CITIES DURING 1971 The regional distribution of suicidal deaths during 1971 showed marked variations from State to State over 1970. The highest increase during 1971 over 1970 was noticed in the State of Gujarat (57·9%) while significant decreases were noticed in Bihar (64·8%) and Uttar Pradesh (34·1%). Among the Union Territories, a substantial number of suicidal deaths were registered in Delhi and Pondicherry and these very Union Territories indicated decreases of 40·8% and 11·3% respectively over 1970. Among the cities, Ahmedabad and Bangalore indicated increases over 1970, the increases being 155·6% and 67·4% respectively, while all other cities under study indicated decreases, a sharp decrease being noticed in Madras 46·4%. The highest number of suicidal deaths were recorded in West Bengal (7.959) followed by Tamil Nadu (5,124), Maharashtra (4,219) and Uttar Pradesh (4,177) and these 4 States together accounted for about 50% of the total suicidal deaths in the entire country. The highest volume of suicidal deaths per one lakh of population was also noticed in West Bengal (17·8) followed by Kerala (15·6), Tripura (12·8). Tamil Nadu (12·4) and Haryana (11·9) as against the All-India average of 7·9. Among the Union Territories the volume of suicidal deaths per one lakh of population was very high in Andaman & Nicobar Islands (55·2), Dadra & Nagar Haveli (28·4), and Pondicherry (46·2).
